title: Virtual agarose gel: simulate a restriction digest online | SeqNexus
description: Run a digest, a PCR product or a whole plasmid on a simulated agarose gel in your browser, against the ladder you use, with a migration model fitted to real gels, and design a diagnostic digest that tells your clones apart. Free, no account.
ogTitle: Virtual agarose gel: simulate a restriction digest online
ogDescription: Digests, PCR products and whole plasmids on a simulated gel with real ladders and a migration model fitted to real gels, plus a diagnostic digest designer. Free, in your browser.
articleDescription: How SeqNexus simulates an agarose gel: lanes and mass, the migration model, how bands spread and merge, ladders, looks and export, and the diagnostic digest designer.
shotAlt: A virtual agarose gel of pEGFP-C1 digests beside a ladder, with the fragment table of the selected lane
h1: A virtual agarose gel that behaves like the real one.
lede: Load a digest, a PCR product or an uncut plasmid, pick your ladder and your agarose percentage, and read the bands before you pour the gel. The migration model is fitted to real gels, the brightness follows the mass, and a designer finds the digest that tells your clones apart. Free, no account, computed on your own machine.
closing: Run the digest before you pour the gel.

title: CRISPR guide design tool, free in your browser | SeqNexus
description: Design CRISPR guides in your browser: protospacers for a dozen nucleases or one you describe, scored for activity, repair outlook and rules, with off-target search using CFD, plus knockout, deletion, knock-in, base and prime editing. Free, no account.
ogTitle: CRISPR guide design tool, free in your browser
ogDescription: Scored protospacers for a dozen nucleases, off-target search with CFD, donors that will not be re-cut, base and prime editing, and the edit read back from a chromatogram.
articleDescription: How SeqNexus designs CRISPR guides: finding sites, the three score columns, the off-target search and its two scoring models, designing for a goal, and reading the edit back.
shotAlt: The CRISPR guide designer with scored guides and the PAM and cut drawn on the sequence
lede: Protospacers for a dozen nucleases or one you describe yourself, kept in three separate score columns so you can see which property a guide fails on. Off-target search over sequences you name, never a genome the tool pretends to have. Tasks for knocking out, deleting, knocking in, base editing and prime editing, and the edit read back afterwards. Free, computed on your own machine.
closing: Pick a guide and check it against what you name.

title: Sanger sequence analysis online: AB1 viewer, assembly, clone checks | SeqNexus
description: Open AB1 and SCF chromatograms in your browser, trim them, assemble reads into contigs against a reference or de novo, and verify a whole plate of clones at once with every mismatch named. Free, no account, nothing uploaded.
ogTitle: Sanger sequence analysis online: AB1 viewer, assembly, clone checks
ogDescription: Chromatograms with quality scores, trimming, contig assembly and plate-scale clone verification, all in the browser with nothing uploaded.
articleDescription: How SeqNexus reads Sanger data: trimming rules, assemblies and contigs, assembling a plate by name against several references, editing inside a contig, and variant effects.
shotAlt: Two Sanger traces of a pEGFP-C1 clone assembled on the plasmid, with a variant called as a missense change
h1: Sanger chromatograms, assembly and clone verification.
lede: Open AB1 and SCF traces with their quality scores, trim them by the rule you choose, assemble them against a reference or de novo, and verify a whole plate of clones in one run with every mismatch named and its protein change worked out. Free, no account, computed on your own machine.
closing: Drag in your traces and verify the plate.

title: Codon optimization tool, free in your browser | SeqNexus
description: Optimize a coding sequence for expression in another host: 19 genetic codes, built-in and imported codon usage tables, restriction sites and motifs avoided, GC and repeat limits, with CAI and GC before and after. Free, no account, nothing uploaded.
ogTitle: Codon optimization tool, free in your browser
ogDescription: Host usage tables, 19 genetic codes, and constraints for restriction sites, motifs, homopolymers, repeats and GC, with the protein guaranteed unchanged.
articleDescription: How SeqNexus optimizes codons: targets and reading frames, genetic codes and usage tables, the constraint set, why the algorithm is greedy with backtracking, and the metrics.
shotAlt: The codon optimization dialog with avoided restriction sites and custom motifs, and CAI and GC before and after
h1: Codon optimization with the constraints your cloning needs.
lede: Rewrite a coding region for another host, keeping the restriction sites your strategy needs free and staying inside what a synthesis vendor accepts. Nineteen genetic codes, host usage tables built in or imported, and the protein guaranteed unchanged. Free, computed on your own machine.
closing: Optimize a gene for your host.

title: Map NGS reads and call variants in your browser | SeqNexus
description: Import FASTQ, read a FastQC-style quality report, trim with fastp, map with minimap2 and call variants with their effect on every coding feature, all in the browser with nothing uploaded. De novo assembly and BAM in and out. Free, no account.
ogTitle: Map NGS reads and call variants in your browser
ogDescription: FASTQ quality control, trimming with fastp, mapping with minimap2, variant calling with HGVS-named coding effects, and de novo assembly, all computed on your own machine.
articleDescription: How SeqNexus handles NGS reads: read set storage and quality control, trimming, mapping with two passes for circular references, variant effects, samples, de novo assembly and measured scale.
shotAlt: A read mapping with coverage track, reads and called variants
h1: Map a FASTQ and call its variants, in a browser tab.
lede: Import a read set, read its quality report, trim it, map it with minimap2 compiled to WebAssembly, and read what every variant does to the coding features it falls in. De novo assembly, several samples per mapping, and BAM in and out. Nothing is uploaded: it all runs on your own machine.
closing: Drag in a FASTQ and map it.

title: Sequence alignment online: MAFFT, MUSCLE and Kalign in your browser | SeqNexus
description: Align sequences in your browser with MAFFT, MUSCLE and Kalign compiled to WebAssembly, or pairwise with Needleman-Wunsch and Smith-Waterman. Editable viewer with conservation, translation and figure export. Free, no account, nothing uploaded.
ogTitle: Sequence alignment online: MAFFT, MUSCLE and Kalign in your browser
ogDescription: Multiple alignment with the real tools compiled to WebAssembly, pairwise alignment in linear memory, and an editable viewer with conservation, translation and figure export.
articleDescription: How SeqNexus aligns sequences: the three WebAssembly engines and when each is chosen, the alignment document and its tracks, how identity is counted, and the built-in pairwise algorithms with their size limits.
shotAlt: A MAFFT alignment of five GFP variants with translation rows and the statistics panel
h1: Multiple and pairwise alignment, in a browser tab.
lede: MAFFT, MUSCLE and Kalign compiled to WebAssembly, chosen automatically by what the job needs, plus pairwise alignment in linear memory for sequences up to tens of kilobases. An editable viewer with conservation, translation and figure export. Free, computed on your own machine.
